name: Full-text search
explanation: Searching large amounts of text by words and relevance rather than exact matches, often tolerating typos.
requirements: Search with a real full-text index, not LIKE with a leading wildcard;Handle typos, plurals and different word forms;Rank results by relevance and highlight the matching words;Debounce search as you type and limit the number of results;Search only data the user may see, or filter the results by permission
done_when: Common misspellings still find the right results;Users never see results they have no access to

name: User comments
explanation: Letting users post, reply to, edit and moderate comments on content such as posts or products.
triggers: comment on;leave a comment;reply to;comments under;add comments;discussion
requirements: Escape or sanitize comment text so it can never run scripts;Rate-limit posting and filter spam;Let authors edit and delete their own comments, and moderators remove any;Paginate or lazy-load long threads;Show a clear error and keep the draft if posting fails
done_when: Posting a script tag shows it as plain text;Users can only edit or delete their own comments, while moderators can remove any

name: Maps and location
explanation: Showing places on an interactive map and finding the user's location, with services such as Google Maps, Mapbox or the browser's Geolocation API.
triggers: show on a map;near me;user's location;where they are;nearest store;distance
requirements: Ask for location only when the user does something that needs it;Handle permission denied, and offer to type a place instead;Restrict map API keys to your own domains;Provide a text list of the locations as well as the map;Do not track location in the background without a clear reason and consent
done_when: Denying location still lets the user find places;Keyboard and screen reader users get the same information without the map

name: PDF generation
explanation: Creating PDF files such as invoices, tickets or reports from app data, on the server or in the browser.
triggers: download as pdf;invoice pdf;print to pdf;create an invoice;printable
requirements: Generate large or slow PDFs in a background job;Use a template so the layout stays consistent;Embed fonts, and test non-Latin characters;Set a title and language, and tag the structure for accessibility;Check permissions before generating or downloading a document
done_when: Generated PDFs look the same in every viewer;Users can only download documents they are allowed to see

name: Data export
explanation: Letting users download data as a file, such as CSV or Excel, often generated in the background for large exports.
triggers: as a spreadsheet;to excel;as csv;download their data;export to;download as
requirements: Export only data the user is allowed to see;Build large exports in the background, and notify the user when ready;Write CSV as UTF-8 with a byte order mark so Excel shows special characters;Prefix cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return with a single quote to stop formula injection;Include clear column headers and the export date
done_when: The file opens correctly in Excel and Google Sheets;Exports never contain data from other accounts

name: Data import
explanation: Letting users upload a file such as CSV or Excel to create many records at once, with validation and a report of rows that failed.
triggers: import from;upload a csv;upload a spreadsheet;import users;many at once;from excel
requirements: Validate every row, and report errors by row and column;Show a preview before importing;Import large files in the background and show progress;Make imports safe to repeat, so importing a file twice creates no duplicates;Limit file size and accept only the expected file types
done_when: A file with some bad rows reports exactly what to fix;Importing the same file again creates no duplicates

name: Analytics and event tracking
explanation: Measuring how people use the app, such as page views, clicks and sign-ups, with tools like Google Analytics, PostHog or Plausible.
triggers: how many users;track clicks;which pages;usage statistics;track visitors;conversion rate
requirements: Ask for consent before tracking where the law requires it;Never send personal data such as emails or names to analytics;Give events clear, consistent names, and document them;Track the events that answer real product questions;Let analytics fail silently without breaking the app
done_when: Key events appear in analytics with the expected properties;No personal data shows up in analytics reports

name: Transactional email
explanation: Automatic emails sent because of something a user did, such as a welcome message, a receipt or a password reset, through a service like SendGrid or Amazon SES.
triggers: send an email;send email;welcome email;confirmation email;email when;receipt email;email the user
requirements: Send emails from a background job with retries;Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for the sending domain;Include a plain-text version as well as HTML;Use templates, and test them in common email apps;Never put passwords in emails, and make any links or codes in them single-use and short-lived
done_when: Emails arrive in the inbox, not in spam;Emails display correctly in major email apps, including dark mode

name: SMS messages
explanation: Sending text messages to users' phones through a provider such as Twilio, for alerts, reminders or verification codes.
triggers: send an sms;text the user;send a text;message their phone
requirements: Get consent, and offer a way to opt out, such as replying STOP;Store phone numbers in the international E.164 format;Rate-limit sending to prevent abuse and high costs;Keep messages short and name the sender;Handle delivery failures and invalid numbers
done_when: Users who opted out receive no more messages;A flood of requests cannot send thousands of messages

name: Online payments
explanation: Taking money from customers through a payment provider such as Stripe or PayPal, including one-off payments, subscriptions and refunds.
triggers: charge customers;take payments;pay online;credit card;monthly plan;subscription;accept payments;refund
requirements: Use the provider's hosted checkout or card fields, so card data never touches your server;Confirm success from a verified webhook, not only from the browser redirect;Use idempotency keys so a retry never charges twice;Store amounts as whole numbers in the smallest unit, such as cents, with a currency;Handle failed payments, refunds and disputes;Ask users to confirm again before sensitive actions, such as changing payout details;Confirm high-risk transactions with a code tied to the amount and payee the user was shown
done_when: Paying works end to end in the provider's test mode;A double click or a retry never creates two charges

name: Filters and faceted search
explanation: Letting users narrow a list of results with filters such as price range, brand or category, often shown in a sidebar with counts.
triggers: filter by;filter products;price range;narrow down;by category;refine results
requirements: Show how many results each filter value has;Keep filter choices in the URL so results can be shared and survive a reload;Update results without losing the scroll position or focus;Offer a clear all filters button;Make filters usable with the keyboard and on small screens;Announce the updated result count to screen readers with a live region
done_when: Applying and clearing filters always gives correct results and counts;Reloading or sharing the URL keeps the same filters
